Read any MSP-like spectral library file

Source: R/read_libraray_functions.R
read_library.Rd

Generic reader for spectral library files regardless of field naming conventions. Accepts Bruker .library, CSU-PMF .mspLib, MoNA .msp, NIST .msp, or any MSP-like plain text format.

This function is permissive — it reads whatever fields are present without normalizing or filtering. Use it as Step 1 of the workflow before convert_to_nist_msp.

For importing already-clean NIST MSP files into your analysis pipeline, use import_msp directly instead.

Usage

read_library(
  file_path,
  dedup_by = "none",
  reserve_n = 10000L,
  max_records = -1L
)

Arguments

file_path

Path to the library file (.msp, .library, .mspLib, .txt).

dedup_by

Deduplication strategy. Default "none" — keep all entries so nothing is lost before conversion. Options: "name_adduct_mode_energy", "name_adduct_mode", "name_only", "none".

reserve_n

Memory hint for expected number of compounds (default 10000).

max_records

Integer. Stop after this many records (-1 = no limit).

Value

A named list of compounds, each containing raw metadata fields and a Peaks data frame (mz, rel_intensity).

See also

convert_to_nist_msp, import_msp

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Step 1a: Read Bruker .library (non-standard fields: IonPolarity, InstName, etc.)
bruker_raw <- read_library("inhouse_library.library")

# Step 1b: Read CSU-PMF .mspLib (SYNON-encoded metadata)
csu_raw <- read_library("CSUPMF_C8_lib.mspLib")

# Step 2: Convert both to clean NIST MSP (run once, then use the .msp files)
convert_to_nist_msp(bruker_raw, "inhouse_library.msp",
                    source_lab = "Your Lab, Your University")
convert_to_nist_msp(csu_raw, "CSUPMF_C8.msp",
                    source_lab = "Broeckling Lab, Colorado State University")
} # }
